labels.label: def:causally_connected

hypotheses.note: DEC-20: an inextensible causal curve (DEC-11/13) over an interval I, in W = ⊤; its image is connected by construction (CausalCurveIn.isConnected_image), so connectedness is not asked separately
read: c s = p, c t = q with s ≤ t (p met first). In a causal spacetime the order is immaterial: causallyConnectedCurves_iff_of_isCausal proves the unordered version equivalent

findings: Under DEC-20 Minkowski space ℝ^{1,n} is causally connected for every n (minkowski_causallyConnectedCurves), where the literal definition fails for n ≥ 1 (minkowski_not_causallyConnected, CausalScaffold.Minkowski). More generally every static spacetime ℝ × X over a geodesic metric space is: through p ≤ q passes the graph of a 1-Lipschitz map — the geodesic segment from p to q prolonged by the vertical lines through p and q — which is inextensible because time is unbounded along it (staticCausality.exists_inextensible_graph).

Negative example (audit): ℚ with the causality of its order (linearCausality ℚ) is not causally connected: ℚ is totally disconnected, so every causal curve is constant (rat_not_causallyConnectedCurves). It is non-local and not causally arc-connected, both proved: rat_not_absolutelyMinimal (the cover by the two sides of √2), rat_not_causallyArcConnected (kb/0019). Under causal arc-connectedness and causality, connectedness follows from CurvesExtend (CauchyExtension.lean:82), here as a hypothesis (causallyConnectedCurves_of_curvesExtend).
questions: OQ-20 (open, mentioned in SCOPE (a)): should causal connectedness also read 'a connected maximal chain of (M, ≤) containing p and q', as completeness does under DEC-21? The ordered reading of 'from p to q' is kept (the paper's plain text; immaterial under causality).

labels.label: def:causally_complete

hypotheses.note: DEC-21 as read by the master session: IsMaxChain (C.le ⊤) S, a totally ordered subset of (M, ≤_M) containing every point comparable to all of S. isMaxChain_iff_comparableClosed proves IsMaxChain is exactly DEC-21's 'every point comparable to all of S lies in S'. For a non-causal C, ≤_M is only a preorder and an IsMaxChain is total for it, not 'totally ordered' in the author's sense (SCOPE (a))

DedekindComplete of Causal.Chains (non-empty parts bounded above in S have a least upper bound in S), proved equivalent for chains to the cut form of DEC-21: every partition S = L ⊔ U, L, U non-empty, L ≤ U, has a greatest element of L or a least element of U (dedekindComplete_iff_cuts)

findings: The master's reading of DEC-21 and the author's literal sentence agree on causal spacetimes: requiring every 'author-chain' (totally ordered; a point cutting S into two NON-EMPTY pieces, strictly below and strictly above, lies in S) to be Dedekind-complete is equivalent to CausallyCompleteOrder (causallyCompleteOrder_iff_author, due to the WP-6b audit).

Under DEC-21 the notion is neither vacuous nor trivial. Maximal chains of (M, ≤) exist through every chain (Zorn, exists_isMaxChain_le) and are not dense. Every maximal chain of Minkowski space ℝ^{1,n} (every n) and of the timelike line is Dedekind-complete (minkowski_causallyCompleteOrder, timelikeLine_causallyCompleteOrder), as is every static spacetime over a complete geodesic space, proper or not (staticCausality.causallyCompleteOrder).

LOCAL negative example: the half-plane ℝ × ]0,∞[ (an open subset of 1+1 Minkowski, its causality of curves; causal, tarentin, strongly causal, causally arc-connected, absolutely minimal). The two null rays t + x = 1 and t − x = 1 form a maximal chain of (M, ≤) (halfPlaneWedge_isMaxChain) whose cut at the missing corner (1, 0) has no bound (halfPlane_not_causallyCompleteOrder).

Relation with the curve reading (b) (CausallyCompleteCurves, ChainsCurves): reading (b) does NOT imply the DEC-21 notion — ℚ with its order is complete for curves (all causal curves constant, rat_causallyCompleteCurves) and not order-complete (ℚ is its own maximal chain, cut at √2, rat_not_causallyCompleteOrder); the witness is non-local and not causally arc-connected (rat_not_absolutelyMinimal, rat_not_causallyArcConnected). Whether the DEC-21 notion implies (b), in general or under DEC-22's hypotheses, is open: both follow from causal compactness under them, both fail on the half-plane, both hold over ℝ × C([0,1], ℝ).

labels.label: rem:causal_completeness_slightly_weaker

hypotheses.note: compact ⇒ complete: causallyCompleteOrder_of_causallyCompact; through closed J^±(x) (prop:GH_Jferme) a non-empty chain bounded above has a least upper bound in M (hasChainSups_of_causallyCompact), comparable to all of any maximal chain containing the part, hence on it

hypotheses.paper: not conversely, for second countable Hausdorff spacetimes (ETT.tex:255) under DEC-22
hypotheses.note: witness ℝ × C([0,1], ℝ): SECOND COUNTABLE (mathlib's ContinuousMap instance), T2, tarentin, causal, causally arc-connected, J^±(p) ≠ {p}, absolutely minimal (local, kb/0014, kb/0019), strongly causal; causally complete (staticCausality.hasChainSups: spatial parts of a bounded chain are Cauchy; C([0,1], ℝ) is complete) and not causally compact (tentStatic_not_causallyCompact: J((0,0),(2,0)) contains (1, tent n), dyadic tents of disjoint support pairwise at distance ≥ 1). It is NOT LOCALLY COMPACT. The earlier witness ℝ × (ℕ →ᵇ ℝ) (bcfStatic_not_causallyCompact, kept) is not second countable

findings: Under DEC-21 and DEC-22 the remark is proved in both halves for second countable Hausdorff spacetimes. 'Compact ⇒ complete' needs only T2, tarentin and causal. The witness of strictness is local and second countable but not locally compact; a locally compact one is not known (the half-plane fails both properties).

Audit correction: the first witness ℝ × (ℕ →ᵇ ℝ) is not second countable (indicators of subsets of ℕ form an uncountable 1-separated set); replaced by ℝ × C([0,1], ℝ) in both not_causallyCompleteOrder_imp_causallyCompact and not_causallyCompleteCurves_imp_causallyCompact, whose quantified class now includes [SecondCountableTopology N].
questions: The witness of 'not conversely' is not locally compact (ℕ →ᵇ ℝ is infinite-dimensional). If the remark is meant in a locally compact setting, a witness is still owed.

labels.label: def:maximal_chain
findings: Superseded by DEC-20: Causal.Chains keeps the literal definition (IsMaximalChain) as the record of the finding (a maximal chain is dense; none exists in Minkowski space). Relation proved here: the image of an inextensible causal curve over ℝ which is an embedding is a subset causal chain (CausalCurveIn.isCausalChain_range), and in ℝ^{1,n}, n ≥ 1, through every p ≤ q passes such a curve whose image is a chain and is not maximal (minkowski_curveChain_not_maximal).

kb_proposals: A completeness or boundedness notion along inextensible curves: reduce to curves over ℝ with Inextensible.reparam (Causal.Cauchy), then use the extension steps of Causal.Geroch (futureExtensible_of_forall_ge / pastExtensible_of_forall_le) or, in static spacetimes over a complete X, tendsto_time_atTop/atBot.

A supremum along a curve: take σ = sSup of the parameters; 'least' goes through IsClosed.csSup_mem on {t ∈ [v, σ] | c t ∈ J^-(c v)}, closed by ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed — no causality needed (CausalCurveIn.exists_isLUBOn).

Cheap local counterexamples: static spacetimes over a non-complete or non-proper geodesic X — the half-plane ℝ × Ioi 0 (geodesicSpace_Ioi_zero) for a curve running into a boundary, ℝ × (ℕ →ᵇ ℝ) for a non-compact diamond (bump n, pairwise at distance 1). Both are absolutely minimal (kb/0014, kb/0019 satisfied).
An anonymous instance cannot be curated (kb/0015): name it (geodesicSpace_Ioi_zero).

Maximal chains of the causal order: mathlib IsMaxChain (C.le ⊤) S (IsChain is Pairwise over x ≠ y of r x y ∨ r y x); to show a point p lies on a maximal chain, prove it comparable to all of S and use hS.2 on IsChain.insert.

Least upper bounds of chains in a causally compact T2 spacetime with closed J^±: IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed (not dot-callable) on t a = J(a₀,u) ∩ J^+(a) ∩ ⋂ upper bounds J^-(v), directed along the chain.
Half-plane computations: write ≤ in null coordinates (halfPlane_le_iff: t+x and t−x both increase) and everything is linarith.

A second countable, complete, non-proper geodesic space for counterexamples: C(Icc (0:ℝ) 1, ℝ) (SecondCountableTopology from ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology, geodesic by GeodesicSpace.ofNormedSpace); dyadic tents `tent n` are 1-separated in the unit ball. ℕ →ᵇ ℝ is NOT second countable.
